findings.claim: The change raises MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000. REQ-2283 is a generator/analyzer crash fix and asks for nothing like this. The change weakens the untrusted-data stack-depth guard: ledger L9 records that a 500-deep limit is deliberate. A 5000-deep hostile payload can now recurse ten times deeper, which risks a StackOverflow DoS that cannot be caught.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test asserting MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500. Also deserialize a 1000-level nested array (0x91 repeated 1000 times, then 0xC0) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData) and expect MessagePackSerializationException. Both pass on base and fail on head.

findings.claim: The requirement names three unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites (reporter lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff guards only the two around new lines 985 and 1077; the first (~line 708 in this file) is untouched. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper does not help there. In `this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(Diagnostic.Create(..., x.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]...))` the argument is built before the wrapper runs whenever reportDiagnostic is non-null, which it is in the analyzer path. That path can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException (AD0001) for a metadata symbol. This breaks the criterion that diagnostics needing a source location do not crash without declaring syntax.

Separately, grep TypeCollector.cs on head for 'DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]'. Any remaining hit inside a reportDiagnostic argument confirms the unguarded path.
